title: Session Affinity Observability Index and Heuristics
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical index and set of heuristics for making session affinity visible across metrics, traces, and dashboards. Focus is on inference flows where session affinity drives cache warmth, token-level tail latency, and feature gating decisions (dedicated vs hosted routing).

Why session affinity matters here (short):
- KV/prefix cache warmth is strongly per-session; small number of warm sessions can dominate latency wins.
- Routing decisions and graceful-fallback behaviors rely on identifying session cold starts.
- Multi-tenant fairness & cost attribution requires session-level metrics to avoid misattributing cold-starts to models or regions.

Quick definitions (canonical names for metric instrumentation):
- session.id: opaque session identifier propagated (SDK header: X-Redwood-Session).
- session.duration_ms: wall-clock lifetime of the session (from first call to explicit end or TTL).
- session.request_count: number of inference requests tied to session.id in window.
- session.kv_warmth_pct: cardinality-normalized fraction of keys present in local KV for a session (0..100).
- session.prefix_reuse_rate: fraction of tokens in new requests that reused existing prefix cache entries.
- session.first_token_latency_ms: latency to first model token for requests from a session (p50/p95/p99).
- session.tail_token_latency_ms: p99+ token latency inside a request, attributed to session context.
- session.model_variant: string tag for model variant (e.g., gptx-8q, gptx-16k-fp16).
- session.tenant_tier: free | standard | enterprise (important for sampling).

Tracing labels and span anchors (recommended tags to add to root span and long-lived spans):
- session.id (high-cardinality, tag but also indexed for span lookup).
- session.kv_warmth_bucket (low-cardinality: cold|warm|hot).
- session.tier (tenant_tier).
- routing.policy (latency|cost|fallback).
- model.variant.
- request.seq_len_bucket (short|medium|long).
- cache.eviction_reason (evicted|ttl|manual).
- note: avoid adding user PII; session.id should be opaque and reversible only by CS tools if needed.

Sampling strategy (practical):
- Head sample (1% overall) for all traces to provide population baseline.
- Session-focused adaptive sampling: keep a sliding window of sessions ranked by session.kv_warmth_pct and latency. If a session exhibits low kv_warmth_pct and rps>threshold, bump traces to 100% for that session for 10 min.
- Tier-aware budget: enterprise sessions have a higher trace budget; free-tier kept at lower baseline to control cost.
- Anomaly-triggered burst: integrate with anomaly detector on session.first_token_latency_p95 to temporarily elevate sampling for related sessions.

Dashboard composition (wireframe notes):
- Landing tile: Session Coldness Leaderboard (top 25 sessions by lowest kv_warmth_pct with request_count > X). Columns: session.id (linkable), tenant, tier, kv_warmth_pct, avg_first_token_latency_p95, request_count, model_variant.
- Heatmap: Session Affinity vs Latency. Rows: top N sessions, Columns: latency quantile buckets (p50/p95/p99) across 15-minute bins. Color by change vs baseline.
- Probe widget: Live session probe (synthetic replay) for selected session.id — shows last 50 requests and span links.
- Cost panel: Request cost by session bucket (cold/warm/hot) with token breakdown; helps justify caching/route decisions.
- Alert panel: Sessions with consistent cold starts (>5 cold starts in 30m) and rising tail latency.
- Operator quickcard: For a selected session show trace links, KV keyset preview (hash list), and actionable buttons (force-evict, pin-model-variant, escalate).

Metric aggregation guidance and SQL snippets (example):
-- Sample: compute session-level kv_warmth_pct over last 1h
-- SELECT session_id, SUM(kv_keys_present)::float / SUM(kv_keys_expected) * 100 as kv_warmth_pct,
--        COUNT(1) as request_count
-- FROM inference_session_kv_events
-- WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval '1 hour'
-- GROUP BY session_id

Open questions / tradeoffs to surface:
- How long should session TTL be for instrumentation? 15m vs 1h impacts cardinality and storage. Recommend 30m initial; re-evaluate after 2 sprints.
- Do we treat multi-tab / multi-device as same session? For product features likely separate, but for caching affinity maybe join on a stable context id.
- Cost: per-session traces can blow up trace volume. Need to enforce tiered budgets and adaptive eviction heuristics.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Instrument session.id header (SDK + gateway) and emit session.request_count and session.first_token_latency_ms. 2 weeks prototype.
2) Add session.kv_warmth_pct and prefix_reuse_rate; wire into tracing tags and low-card buckets. 3 weeks.
3) Build leaderboards and heatmap widgets in dashboard sandbox; validate with 2 customers (internal). 2 weeks.
4) Enable adaptive sampling and alerting (increase budgets for enterprise). 2 weeks.

Operational playbook excerpts (short):
- Investigation steps for high tail latency: 1) Filter traces by session.id on p99 requests. 2) Check kv_warmth_pct and prefix_reuse_rate. 3) If kv_warmth_pct < 20% and request_count < 10 => cold start behavior. 4) If kv_warmth_pct < 20% and request_count > 100 => eviction pathology; check node GC/eviction logs.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add a lightweight session cardinality gauge to monitor storage impact.
- Prototype an "intentional skirt" synthetic that warms session prefixes for internal canaries.
- Sync with serving-runtime on eviction_reason tag semantics (Miguel).
- Wire Confluence page with decision log: CONFLUENCE-OBS-452 (linked).

References and related artifacts:
- CONFLUENCE-OBS-452: session affinity decision log (work-in-progress)
- JIRA-OBS-1734: Implement session header + SDK propagation
- PR: https://github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/221: initial session-id instrumentation

If you want a compact checklist for an oncall quick drill, tell me and I will extract a one-page runbook and example queries.
